utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. Welcome back to these proceedings. Judge El Mahdi won't be able to join us today and tomorrow, so in accordance with Rule 15(B) the remaining Judges decided to continue our proceedings. Before we hear the witness, are there any matters that the parties would like to raise? Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just two brief matters, Your Honour. One is with regard to Enver Mujezinovic. As we notified you at the Status Conference, he is being withdrawn from our list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any comments on that, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, in light of the rulings that Your Honours made in the past concerning the Prosecution's ability to withdraw witnesses, we don't seek to add anything to that. We do regret being put to the work, but at the same time Your Honours have ruled on any substantive matters that I would want to raise and I have nothing to add to it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your cooperation. This witness is withdrawn from the witness list.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. The next matter concerns actually an ongoing request by the Court to try and limit or to try and 89(F) or 92 bis witnesses as much as possible. As the Court knows, the first pathologist of the two we used the 89(F) system or process, and were able to move quickly through that request and get her completed within one day. The next witness is also a pathologist. He has filed extensive autopsy reports. He has a witness statement and he has provided proofing notes yesterday. So it is our plan, and I mentioned it to the Defence -- in fact, the Defence a few weeks ago suggested that we 89(F) -- or maybe three weeks ago suggested that -- and we are in fact going to 89(F) the witness. We are making the request to the Court to use the 89(F) process. We would put those three documents in. The only testimony would be, other than background, have him explain some medical concepts which are in fact in the different various reports, and then turn him over for cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I hear the comments from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This witness is an expert and is giving evidence within his field of expertise. He has provided an extensive statement and also we have the reports and have had them for a long time. I'm not sure of the status of the proofing notes in the 89(F) situation here. And in particular, I'm not sure whether they've been signed or what the position is with respect to them. But generally speaking, we agree and we encourage this approach to be taken. There will be some significant cross-examination -- or not short cross-examination. Whether it's significant is a matter for the Court to decide. But there will be some cross-examination that happens. We may finish him today, it's possible. Probably finish him tomorrow within, you know, half an hour, perhaps an hour at the most. So we agree to that but I'm just wondering if it would be possible to clarify what the situation with the proofing notes is. Certainly as to the statements and the reports, I'm -- I do agree to those being tendered under 89(F).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. The witness arrived after lunch today. I've shown him the proofing notes, he agrees to them. I can have him sign them right here and introduce those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So the Prosecution's request is granted by this Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Your Honour, there's a matter that the Defence has to raise. We've indicated to the Prosecutors by a letter that we would raise it and now we do. This concerns the expert -- I describe, unfortunately, as the alleged expert, Mr. Ridgway. Your Honours, by a letter dated the 10th of May, the Defence continued a chain of requests to the Prosecutor to clarify what the situation was with the expert that they propose to call. That's Major General or Lieutenant General Ridgway, and then the Prosecution responded by a letter dated the 12th of May, indicating as follows, and we have to put this on the record now, what the Prosecution have indicated, because we take it very seriously, we oppose what's proposed, and we think there are some very serious issues raised by it. What's been indicated to us here is that the Prosecution does intend to call General Ridgway. That's the first step. Secondly, the Prosecution say they want to -- they intend to tender the existing report. Next, they say they would not highlight -- they would not rely on certain portions highlighted in yellow to the annexed copy. I should indicate that an annexed copy has been given to us with certain parts of it highlighted in grey. That will be a function of our printer rather than the Prosecutor's colour-blindness. So we know what parts they say they don't want to rely on. They then go on to say this: "We will blank out these parts from the tendered copy and have the general adopt the remainder." Now, that's what's proposed, apparently, by the Prosecution. The Prosecution have gone on to say this: "General Ridgway is the chief of military intelligence for the United Kingdom. He has an extremely limited time to testify and he's only available in the foreseeable future to testify on 25 May. They indicate a contact they have had with the Chamber's legal officer in an attempt to extend that time period to make it an all-day session. The Prosecution also indicate that there is some further materials or further evidence that needs to be led. Firstly, it's indicated here: "We would anticipate leading brief oral evidence from the general in relation to several aspects of his report." It's not explained what they are. The Prosecution also says, and I'm jumping a paragraph here just in order to keep this as coherent, if I can. The Prosecution also says they intend to lead additional oral evidence from him on the specific measures that a commander should take to prevent breaches of international humanitarian law. They say: "We will provide you with notes in the next week of the effect of his proposed testimony on this point and concerning any other additions to his report. We expect," says the Prosecutor, "his evidence on failure to prevent to accord with our pleadings in the indictment and the pre-trial brief on these matters." Now, that's what the Prosecution have indicated to us, and I've got some responses that I have to make to it now and to indicate further responses that we are going to make. But, Your Honours, I have to call on the Prosecutor before I go any further to answer a couple of questions, and the first one is: Has Major General Ridgway seen the addendum with the parts to be deleted? Secondly, has he agreed to sign such a document that has been cut? Thirdly, are the deletions there deletions of the Prosecutor or of Mr. Ridgway? And finally, it's probably the question that should be asked first, have they spoken to him at all in person? And we need answers to those questions before we go any further, so I ask for those to be answered, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner, are you in a position to answer those questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Mr. Re has handled that matter, would be in a position. However, what we would request is that we have a witness sitting out here and they've indicated that they would only spend maybe a half-hour or so tomorrow. Can we deal with the witness and then maybe spend an hour going back and forth fighting as to this issue tomorrow, rather than having a witness sit there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, is that an urgent matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It is, Your Honours, because the way things are proposed by the Prosecutor, they want to lead their expert evidence through expertise that is as yet undiscovered to us. On the 25th, which is 14 days away, our arrangements have to be made, if they're permitted, and we're going to be moving that they not be allowed to call this witness at all, I can indicate that. But depending on how things work, the fact is we have to make our arrangements in a hurry. And so it is a matter of urgency. I must say I'm entirely in Your Honours' hands as to whether you want to hear this now. We want it dealt with today; we don't want it to be put off. It's -- we've got some harsh comments to make and some submissions we have to make about this; we can do it at the end of today; we can do it now. The Prosecution case is nearly finished and we have been asking for this for months. I understand there's a witness there, and it's with regret that I raise it, but the Defence just finds itself in an impossible position as a result of this. So if Your Honour is minded to hear it at the end of the day, of course we'll cooperate with whatever Your Honour thinks is appropriate in these circumstances, but urgency is upon us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe Mr. Re could answer the questions you put to him today and you might save your harsh argument for tomorrow when we finish the present witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it would ease my mind if he answered those questions right now. It wouldn't take very long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Perhaps if we could have those answers and then put the argument tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The questions are: Firstly, has the Major General seen the addendum with the parts to be deleted? Well, yes, we sent him a copy of the report with the highlighted portions, which we say that in the light of the evidence given in the trial and the documents originally provided to him, that we could not rely upon as part of his testimony. So the answer to that is: Yes, the lieutenant general has an identical copy of the document given to the Defence and the Chamber's legal officer. Secondly, has he agreed to sign such document that has been cut? I don't understand what is meant by "cut." There is nothing at all abnormal about an expert amending a report in the light of changes to evidence between when an original report is made and when a later one is done. So the answer to that is the lieutenant general has not given any indication one way or the other. The Prosecution has merely said that we would not rely upon those portions of the report, in exactly the same way as we would say we would not rely upon portions of a Rule 92 bis statement or an affidavit which are no longer relevant to the proceedings. And most particularly here, in relation to the failure to the prevent Uzdol, obviously that part of his report is not relevant to these proceedings and cannot be relied upon. So the answer to the second question is no. Thirdly, are the deletions of the Prosecutor or of Mr. Ridgway? Clearly -- my learned friend knows that, clearly they are the Prosecutor's. The Prosecutor looking at the document and saying we can't rely upon these parts of the report when we call him to give evidence. So I hope that assists, but we are still mystified by any submission that could be made attacking this particular general's expertise and the right of the Prosecutor to call whoever it likes as it - as long as they are qualified - as its military expert. And I add for the purposes of today's proceedings, that nothing in that letter is in any way different to any indication that we have previously given the Trial Chamber and the Defence as to the procedure to be adopted and the fact that we're going to call the general. We've just put it in writing because they asked us yet again the same questions, which we have answered several times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. That's three questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The fourth one is: Have they spoken to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The answer to that is yes, but it's only administrative.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What do you mean by "administrative"?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To get him here. There's no -- not in any great substance, touching briefly upon the fact that parts of the report can't be relied upon and we would require oral evidence on the issue, as is pointed out in the report -- the letter, that is, the failure to prevent, and we will be in touch fairly soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that tomorrow after we finish the witness we have plenty of time to discuss these matters in detail. There's two rulings concerning of the admission of the documents I would like to make at this stage. The first one is about the document MFI 236. On the 15th April 2005, the Defence filed a motion for the admission of evidence, in which the Defence requested the admission of document MFI 236. This document previously has been tendered through Witness Jusuf Jasarevic on the 4th of March, 2005, but it was not admitted by the Trial Chamber in its oral rulings on the 30th March 2005, without prejudice for further application for the admission. During the trial hearing of the 10th March 2005 the Prosecution did not object to the admission of this document. In its motion, the Defence requests that this document now be admitted based on the evidence presented by Witness Nermin Eminovic. This witness testified that he had received this report and had sent the information to his superior. The Defence, on March 11, did not tender this document through the witness Eminovic because it was understood that it was already admitted. The document contains information as to a number of relevant issues, including information concerning the deaths of one of the alleged victims, Slavko Mendes, in the attack on Uzdol. The Trial Chamber, based on the evidence of witness Eminovic, found that the document MFI 236 is relevant and has probative value and therefore grants Defence motion for admission of evidence filed on the 15th April 2005 and admits this document into evidence. It is so decided. Another oral decision is about agreed facts. The Trial Chamber will now decide on a motion re: agreed facts and the motion for withdrawal of motion for judicial notice on the 22nd of April 2005. In the motion, the Defence submits that on the 21st April 2005 the Prosecution and Defence met and agreed upon a number of proposed facts from the Galic and the Martinovic judgements, which were attached in annexes A and B to the motion. The Defence requests the Trial Chamber to regard those facts as having been agreed upon by the parties. The Defence also seeks leave to withdraw its previous motion for judicial notice filed on the 29th February 2005. Rule 65 ter (H) is intended to promote agreement between the parties and to narrow down the scope of factual and legal issues that will be litigated to points regarding which the parties are in dispute. The agreed facts are accepted into the proceedings and a matter to which the agreed facts relate ceases to be a disputed issue. Rule 65 ter (M) provides that the Trial Chamber may proprio motu exercise any of the functions of the Pre-Trial Judge. The Trial Chamber therefore finds there's no obstacles for it to record points of agreement of parties at the trial stage. The Trial Chamber is of the opinion that the recording of points of agreed -- of agreement between the parties at the trial stage results in the acceptance of those agreed points as evidence under Rule 89(C). For those reasons, the Trial Chamber recalls the agreement of the parties regarding the facts set out in the annex (A) and (B) to the motion. The Trial Chamber also grants leave for the Defence to withdraw its motion for judicial notice of 29th February 2005. Lastly, the Trial Chamber admits the two annexes of the motions into the evidence and requests the registrar to assign one Defence exhibit number to the two annexes. It is so decided. Well, I believe this is the moment for us to have the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, pursuant to the oral order just announced, exhibit numbers for the two annexes will be Exhibit D408.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Would you state your name, please.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon. My name is Simun Andjelinovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you do for work.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a doctor and I have two specialisations; one is forensic medicine and the other is pathology. At the moment I'm working at the pathology department of the Split clinical hospital. I am the head of the department. I have 77 employees who work under me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to ask you some leading questions to move through your background very quickly. You have a degree in medicine and a Ph.D. in forensic medicine. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You serve as a professor of pathology and forensic pathology?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. As I said before, I specialise in pathology and forensic medicine and I teach at the faculty of medicine. I teach pathology and I teach forensic medicine at the faculty of law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have served as author or co-author of some 30 articles relating to pathology and forensic pathology. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are articles that were published in international publications, but I have many more publications, more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have lectured several times in the United States as well as in Croatia, Slovenia, Italy, Austria, and Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I'm a member of international associations for forensic medicine; the American Academy for Forensic Medicine, for example, as well as the Society of Pathologists of Europe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've performed over 2800 autopsies. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, at least that many so far.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's move to September 17th, 1993. Where were you working at that time?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, I was working at the Split clinical hospital at my department, and I was at the head of the department as well as a pathologist specialist and a specialist in forensic medicine.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on that date were some 27 bodies transported from Uzdol for your examination?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you and a team begin autopsies on that date?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I did and I also wrote that down in the records.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Who performed the autopsies?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I, with my team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as a result of these post-mortem examinations, were any reports drafted?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Already in the course of the autopsy, I dictated certain data and findings, after which all of that was recorded and I went over what was recorded. And after I did that, I signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to show you Exhibit 65 ter 137, which has an ERN number of 0105-7135 through 0105-7279.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 409.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it on your screen, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you go to the next page or the pages with the writing, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you start scrolling -- could the registrar start scrolling to the autopsy reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first autopsy report is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could I just intervene very briefly here. As I indicated, I don't object to the autopsy reports going in. Some of the pages that are currently on the screen are correspondence with other individuals. I don't know that they connect to this witness at all. I didn't understand the Prosecutor was going to be tendering these. It may be that in the break we can discuss that. I don't -- I had -- I just don't have a position about it yet. I didn't think it was going to be tendered, so I don't object to, of course, the autopsy reports themselves, which I understand my friend to be going to, but it's just there's four pages of material here which is probably irrelevant and not what the Prosecutor is going to, but perhaps he can tell us what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We can meet at the break and discuss those initial matters. What I think it might be easier, let me just hand a book, which is page 10 to 154 in English and the tenth page in B/C/S. If he can just confirm that those are the autopsy reports.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Starting with number 01057145, those are the copies of my original reports that I drafted during the external examination and post-mortem of the bodies that were brought from Uzdol, a total of 27 of them. And they go up to the page number -- just give me a moment here, please -- 01057279. These pages correspond to the reports that I drafted during the external examination on post-mortem on the 17th of September, 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, did you provide the information that went into those autopsy reports, the medical information?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I participated in drafting these reports. And after the external examination and post-mortem, I provided information that went into the reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the information that's contained, is that accurate to the best of your knowledge, information, and belief?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Some of the information contained at the beginning of the report with regard to the name, the date of birth, the day and time of death was provided to us by third persons, the persons who had brought the bodies to us. As for the professional part of the reports, those were drafted during the external examination of the bodies and post-mortem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and that's the information I'm interested in. The medical observations and conclusions contained therein, are those true and accurate to the best of your knowledge, information, and belief?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I did them to the best of my knowledge, and I fully believe that this information is accurate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to show you a copy of a statement dated 16 April 2002. Are you familiar with that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I gave this statement during the interview with Mr. Brun Bernard in Split in my office in the Split clinical hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the information that you provided, is that also accurate to the best of your knowledge, information, and belief?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This information is correct and it is in keeping with the reports of the external examination and post-mortem that I have mentioned and that you showed a copy of to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd like to offer that at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, in keeping with what we said earlier on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P410.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to now show you the Prosecutor's proofing notes, which are dated yesterday, dated as of yesterday's date, 11 May 2005.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen those before?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I saw these notes while I was preparing for this testimony and I fully agree with the things that I have said and that are recorded herein.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please sign and date those notes, please.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could we offer that, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honours, as long as the witness is asked the question that he -- and gives the answer that he speaks English well enough to understand that document, then of course we don't have any objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Usually proofing notes are not admitted into the evidence, but in this case we will make an exceptional ruling on that. It is admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: With a separate number on it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, do you speak English, Dr. Andjelinovic?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, yes, I speak English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P411.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, the information that you were to testify to today are your 27 autopsy reports, your 2002 statement, your Prosecutor's proofing notes; is that the information that you plan to give to this Chamber today?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, all of this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like to show you one last item. It is a book of photographs, and this is if the Court would like to see the photographs. They're mentioned in the autopsy reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The book that we provided to the Defence had pictures from Grabovica and other matters which we've removed, so it's strictly the 20 pictures taken during the 27 autopsies which relate to this witness. The photograph numbers in the system, in the LiveNote system is 0 -- in the e-court system is 0361-7328 through 0361-7483. Apparently they're not in the e-court system; they've been given those ERN numbers, but it should be in next week.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise those photographs, sir?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [No verbal response].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When were those photographs taken?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise all of these photos and they correspond to the originals that I have with me and that were taken during the autopsies. During the interview, Mr. Bernard took those photos from me, and as I say, he photocopied all of them, so I can say that these photos are identical.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We'd like to offer those, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And the question is: Should we have one number for all those photos or each for one number?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One number for all those photos. They have a separate ERN number on each photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P412.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, in your report you describe gunshot wounds and various locations or ranges of the weapon which fired a gunshot wound. You described the marking that a gunshot wound would make. If I gave you a sheet of paper, could you show us or draw on a piece of paper the different types of wounds based on what you called close and absolute, close wounds, intermediate, and relatively close wounds, and long-range or distance wounds. If we gave you some sheets of paper and if we use the ELMO machine, could you just show us what you were referring to in the different distances and ranges.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would gladly do that because this is very important for the understanding of my descriptions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Is there any possibility for the witness to draw it on the e-court system?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yeah, if it could be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We could try that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If it could be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Let's try that first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Try this first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we see this as the barrel of a firearm from which a bullet is being fired, after the bullet leaves the barrel, together with the bullet there is also gunpowder particles moving together with the bullet, and parallel with them there is also fire which is created during the combustion, and also the bullet moves along with that. Every bullet has its shape, and it will all depend on where the skin is posing an obstacle to the bullet that is moving at a high speed. So an absolute-range wound is a wound which was inflicted from between 0 centimetres and 5 centimetres from the barrel point of the firearm. This wound will be star-shaped, it will be irregular, and at the bottom of the wound we will have -- we will find burns due to fire and we will also find dirt caused by gunpowder particles. Such an entry wound is called an absolute closeness wound, and it is usually much bigger than the exit wound inflicted by the same bullet. A range between 5 centimetres and any other distance which depends on the characteristics of the firearm and can be up to 1 metre, we can see wounds on the body which is circular in shape. However, since there are also gunpowder particles inflicting wound, there is a trace of gunpowder around the wound in the shape of a tattoo. That's why this wound looks different than the wound that was inflicted from a very close range and has very different, very important characteristics of its own. And finally, the last type of wound, that is the entry wound, would be a far-range wound, which is also circular. And in its middle inner part, it has the so-called contusion ring, the diameter of which could be 1 or 2 millimetres; that is its thickness. What is important for this type of wound inflicted from a distant range is that it is most commonly circular if the bullet passes through the skin at the right angle. However, if the bullet enters the skin under a different angle, then this wound can be oval and the contusion ring in this case is more pronounced in one part and less pronounced in another part. What happens to the bullet when it actually enters the body? Its kinetic energy, which is proportional to its speed, is transported across the surrounding tissue. This tissue starts vibrating due to its elasticity. And because of the transfer of energy, the surrounding tissue starts breaking up. In addition to that, the bullet will also encounter a bone. The bone will break up or shatter. And its fragments that originate from that action assume kinetic energy of their own and they continue moving and they also cause damage to the tissue. This is what we called secondary projectiles. When the bullet hits a bone, this may cause the deformity of the bullet and it can split into two or even more fragments which will continue moving as secondary projectiles. After this, the bullet continues moving to the point where it will exit the body. And now something has to be said about the exit wound, which appears as the result of the break-up of the skin and subcutaneous tissue. This exit wound has the following characteristics: It is star-shaped; however, unlike the previous three entry wounds, the skin and the tissue is pushed forward and the wound, when it is pushed back, can be almost completely closed. That is why we call this an adaptable borders or an adaptable wound. As one can see from my drawing, every educated forensic pathologist, based on the traces of -- on a dead body can make a distinction between an entry wound and an exit wound. Another thing that needs to be emphasised is the fact that in forensic pathology we also see explosive wounds inflicted by firearms. Such wounds are a result of the explosion or eruption of an explosive device. When this happens, we have fragments of various shapes that separate from the body of explosive device. These fragments move in various directions away from the explosive device. Unlike a projectile, particles of an explosive device are of an irregular shape and that is why, when they encounter the human tissue, due to their shape and form they will very soon transmit their kinetic energy onto the human tissue. That is why they're -- the channel through which they pass will, as a rule, be much shorter. A wound that is inflicted by such an irregular object will also have an irregular shape and it will have a different set of characteristics. Around the edges of that wound we will see contusion spots and also we will see gunpowder particles and dirt which travels -- which travel together with the fragments of the explosive device. That is why an explosive wound has different characteristics on the tissue than the wounds previously mentioned. What happens after that, and what is interesting from the pathology point of view, what happens to the bullet that has entered the body. For example, a bullet fired from a Kalashnikov, from an automatic rifle, when this bullet enters the skin, it travels for 16 centimetres in a very straight line. And after that, it starts rotating, and finally it exits the body. In some other types of weapons and bullets, for example AK-47 rifle, we have a bullet which in its upper part has air. When such a bullet hits the skin, it starts moving forward so that its trajectory through the body changes and rotation starts immediately after the bullet has entered the body. And that is why this type of bullet causes more serious damage in the body and that is why such a projectile causes bone fracture, and that's why it is often referred to as a bone-breaker.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, on the bottom right could you write "bullets" of the Kalashnikov and the AK-47 bullets on the bottom right so we know there are four different or three different -- actually, four different pictures.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this would be a Kalashnikov bullet, this would be an AK-47.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And below AK-47 could you write "bullets," please, write the word "bullets."

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Could you write it in English, too.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, to the left of that, to the picture, could you write "explosive."

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the middle could you write "bullet entry wounds" in relation to the top left -- the middle left.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then on the top -- the middle right, could you write "exit wounds."

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in the middle can you write "bone breaking" or "bone shattering."

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could we offer that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before that, you may ask this witness to sign this chart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you could do it on the lower right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. There's no objections from the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: So it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P413.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise because of my handwriting. It's not the prettiest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's fine, much better than mine. Now I would like to show you some photographs from Exhibit P14, which are the photos that were just admitted, three photos on Sanction. You just described various wounds and I'd like to show you. The first photograph is 0361-7381. That's from victim number nine. Of the three types of wounds, which is that and why?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] There is no picture now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This would be absolutely close-range wound. This would be the first one in my diagram because the mouth of the barrel was placed very close to the skin, so that the wound is star-shaped, it's of an irregular shape. And we said that in that case the entry wound is larger than the exit wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to show you another one, from victim 18, which is photograph 0361-7425.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: If we look at the diagram, this would be a wound we described as a relatively close-range wound, where along the edges of the wound you see that tattoo effect by the gunpowder particles that I spoke about. And that would indicate that the mouth of the barrel was further away from the skin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now the final one I want to show you is from victim 19, photograph 0361-7435.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: This would be an exit wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Could you explain why that's an exit wound, sir.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: This is an exit wound which, according to my recollection -- I will take a look at the whole report, if you allow me. In case number 19, this exit wound is very characteristic because we have two entry wounds and one exit wound here. The bullets or the projectiles which entered the body of victim number 19 are -- belong to a narrow group. Actually, they -- their point of impact is pretty close to one another and this is quite characteristic of bursts of fire, and you can see that on my original photographs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could -- I'll show you this photograph, and could you look at that from -- it's the same one you have in your hand.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: It is the same photograph that I'm talking about. Could you please zoom in a little bit because I can see it quite well but perhaps the rest of the parties in the court cannot see it that well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have it on the ELMO. If you want to look at the Sanction system, if you want to try the Sanction, we have it pretty good.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We can place it like this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's --

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: These are two entry wounds caused by projectiles of long range, and they are very close to each other, just a few centimetres apart. Their trajectory is similar and that is why victim 19, with him we have the case that they ended up in the same exit wound and that is why this exit wound is a little bit larger than is usual. It's also larger because we're talking about the chest cavity where the projectiles struck the ribs, causing secondary projectiles, and thereby, as a result, creating a larger exit wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, sir, with regard to some of your -- some of the wounds that you've seen, such as the intermediate wounds, you've indicated an area that you think the gun was fired from. As opposed to just saying it was a relatively close-range wound of 5 centimetres to 1 metre, you say within that that it was closer to the 10 centimetres, or 10 to 20, or closer to the 5 centimetres. How do you make that determination?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: If we can go back to my diagram -- maybe we can put it up on the screen. You can see very simply that these categories which we use in forensic medicine in order to differentiate different wounds are quite --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can we go back to his diagram, 413?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have it. These categories are arbitrary and we use them just for sake of orientation. But as a lay person, you could see that it's not the same whether the skin was 5 centimetres or 1 metre away from the flame and the gunpowder particles, and that is why with a quite high degree of probability we can talk about distance if we know what kind of a weapon was used. However, if we would like be very specific, then the weapon in question should be fired in lab conditions so that different distances from the mouth of the barrel can be tested by placing a white sheet in front of the mouth of the barrel, and that is exactly how we would establish the characteristics and the -- of the weapon and the shape of the wound that would be caused on the body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: So I am not speaking with 100 per cent certainty, but based on my experience I think that we could be talking about close wounds up to 5 centimetres and intermediate ones which would be up to 1 metre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: First, for the record, Your Honour, the photograph that was shown to the witness that had the two long-distance entry wounds was 0361-7436.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you performed a complete examination or an internal examination on the first victim, Stjepan Zelic, but on the other 25 you just did external and some partial internal, maybe of the brains, examination. Why did you not complete full internal examinations on all 27 victims?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I started out with the idea of making all of the autopsy reports. However, at that point we were short of time. The autopsies had to be conducted, because of the war and also because of the customs in that area, this had to be done in one day. I was the only forensic expert in that time in Split - my colleague was away - and in order to do that it would have taken too long for us to conduct all of the autopsies, because we saw that based on the first example because the autopsy took much longer and it would not have been possible for us to process all of the victims in the same way. Other than that, the wounds on the bodies of the other victims were such that I could establish the precise cause of death without an internal examination. And for that reason, I believe that the external examination of the victims was sufficient. We started to work at 8.30 in the morning and finished at around 10.00. So if we had worked at a slower pace, we could not have managed to do all of that in one day, and that was the request of the local authorities as well as of the families of the victims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You indicated in the record that you finished around 10.00. Is that 10.00 in the morning or 10.00 in the evening?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. This was at 10.00 in the evening. The same day but 10.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, even though you did external examinations, what is your level of certainty as to your conclusions as to cause of death?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm 100 per cent certain because I would not have signed the permission for burial, that would be the permit based on which the cause of death is recorded. Because the wounds were such that any pathologist would be able to recognise them for what they were, and based on these wounds the cause of death could be established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to show you a piece of a video of Exhibit P312 at 36 minutes and 38 seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're not getting this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We are not getting it, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We're just going to isolate on a picture. That's all we want right there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is Ruza Zelic -- I'm sorry, Zelenika. And you had indicated that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It's on the Sanction. It should be under --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It's still not there?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Try "Computer Evidence."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You should have it now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had indicated a cause of death as a result of being shot and also a hatchet or an axe or some sort of object was used. If you want to look at your report number -- report number 6, Ruza Zelenika.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Just one moment, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, looking at that pattern of the victim lying in bed, does that have any effect on your opinion, the splattering pattern behind her head?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the autopsy findings, I established that the head wound was actually a cut, cutting wound. And that implies a powerful mechanical item, like an axe or any similar item. Based on the way the wound looks, which I examined and as the way it is shown on the picture, and I can show you what I mean. Could you please help me? Could you please zoom in? This is not the best image, but you can see two wounds where you can see contusions on the edges of the wound. These would be the bruising of the tissue caused by an object, which along with a sharp edge has also a blunt edge, which would cause bruising of the tissue. As far as the splattering effect is concerned that we see on the wall, I must say that the head is a part of the body that is very well supplied with blood and that is why, when we have head injuries, the bleeding is quite severe, the blood vessels shatter or burst, and under pressure they can result in the splattering that we have seen on this video image. What is missing here, what is not seen on the video footage, perhaps, is whether we can see whether there were any particles of tissue on the wall as well. This would be brain tissue or skin tissue. And if this were the case, then we could allow for the possibility that some of the injuries were caused also by a projectile. I stand by my assertion that the two wounds on the forehead were caused by a mechanical implement resembling an axe or something like that which also cause bruising of the tissues with their sharp edge. In view of the fact that bones are missing from this rest, it's possible that a projectile was the cause of the injury, but subsequently.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If -- let me ask you two questions off that. If it was a projectile, meaning a gunshot wound, how close or far would the gun be to the head? Basically, is it a close wound, an intermediate wound, or a distance wound?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: In that case, the -- this -- it would be an absolutely close wound because a wound of this type cannot be caused by a projectile from a distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And finally, you indicated that there were -- she was shot to the body -- there were four entrance and exit wounds on the body and that the head wounds occurred after the gunshot wounds to the body. Could you explain that.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: That can be explained as follows: All the wounds were caused while the victim was still alive. How do we see that? We see that by the traces found along the edges of the wound where we see contusions. Contusions can never been caused on the body if it is already dead; there is no vital reaction in that case. The edges of the wound in that case look quite different. For the purposes of making myself more understandable, I can show you a photograph which I brought with me which is also a part of this group of photographs, where you can see a wound caused post-mortem, after death, where you can see that some animals, small animals ate the flesh from the arm of the victim. And underneath the skin, as well as in the muscles, you can see that there are no traces of contusion or bleeding. In forensic medicine, this is something that we call vital reaction, and that is a reaction which is a consequence of the blood flowing through our veins and other reactions of the body. So if we go back to the wound that we were looking at previously, and that is victim number 6, it is possible even to the layperson that after the wound sustained to the head, the victim cannot remain alive after sustaining such a wound. The death would be instantaneous, and that is why I believe that the gunshot wounds were caused first and then the other injuries to the head, following which the victim died very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. No further questions. I would supply, during the break, the two ERN numbers for those two photographs that the witness referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I believe that it's time for us to take and break, and we'll resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. Cross-examined by Mr. Morrissey:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Doctor. Doctor, could I just ask you, do you have the notes and the reports that you made in front of you there?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Can I just indicate to you that when you're giving your evidence here, you may feel free to refer to those at any time. You don't need to ask permission to do that. And furthermore, you may also feel free to refer to other matters in the reports, if they arise out of questions. Now, could I first of all ask you to go to report number 23. That concerns the deceased man Martin Ratkic.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, with respect to Mr. Ratkic, would you please just look at the following video that's going to be shown. This is at Exhibit 3 -- P373, it's V000-2632-1. And the time that we're asking be shown is at 01.40.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is going to be shown by the Prosecutor, who has agreed to show this. May I just ask that that be played, and I'll ask that it be frozen at a certain moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, do you have there in front of you now a depiction of a man in a crouching position?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Just looking at that photograph there, does it appear to you that that man has got a right ear?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I must admit that the picture is not very clear, but I believe that you are right and that this man does have the ear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Look, I understand and I accept your reservation about the view that you have of that picture. We've had sworn evidence in this court about that from a British reporter who took that, and she indicated that there was clearly an ear as well. What I want to ask you is: By the time you came to look at Martin Ratkic, according to your report, that ear was gone, wasn't it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the ear was missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain what happened to that ear?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: When I was briefed by the Prosecutor, I looked at a photograph of the right ear. And maybe it would be good for us to put it on the ELMO. This photo is among the photocopies of my original pictures. You can see the right ear clearly in that photo that I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, do you have those photographs there? Because I've got a copy of the photo.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] I prefer ... [Interpretation] What I would like to say, based on this photo, is the fact that the right ear, judging by this photo, had been removed. But that happened after the death of this person. Around the edges, we don't see any signs of contusion. And that's how we know that the person was dead when the ear was removed. I can't say with any precision what happened between the period when the person died and when the ear went missing. There are two possibilities: One is that somebody removed the ear on purpose or that little rodents such as mice or maybe a cat or similar animals had eaten the ear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As to that second possibility, though, the intervention of small animals, in respect of another individual you were very cautious and clear in pointing out the intervention of that animal, and I'm referring to the bite on one of the limbs that you showed earlier. And therefore, can I ask you this: Had there been the possibility of animal intervention in respect of this individual, you would have noticed that, wouldn't you, rather than using the term "amputated," as you did. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that I would not have used the term, however "amputation" equals removal. So "amputation" is not a wrong term irrespectively of whether the ear was removed by a person or some animals. This is not a term that would indicate who the doer of this action was. As I'm looking at this photo here, due to the irregular edges of the wound, one could opt for the second possibility rather than the first one. It would be easy to conclude that post-mortem small animals were those that removed the ear. And as for the right [as interpreted] ear, maybe we could show that photo as well. The ear in question was removed during the life of the person because one can see contusions within the removed part of the ear and you can also see the remains of the ear in its lower part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, well, we'll come back to the left ear in just a moment. At the moment I want to stick with the right ear. Did you use the specific term in relation to the right ear as follows: "The right ear was completely amputated." Perhaps -- I'll ask you to go to your report on this topic and go to the heading "Opinion" in the final paragraph.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does the second and third sentences read this way: "The external examination also found out that both ears had been amputated. The right ear was completely amputated but the left only partially." Let me ask you this: Why did you say that the right ear was completely amputated?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Because of what I found there. The whole ear was missing. "Amputation" means removal, which could be partial or complete, and in this case we are looking at a complete amputation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it -- but you don't suggest that "amputation" is not a technical term, is it -- well, perhaps I'll put the question to you another way: "Amputation" is a technical term, isn't it, especially in the hands of a doctor. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: In the narrow sense of the word. However, "amputation" means removal and does not imply the mechanism of that removal. As you can see here, I never mentioned the mechanism by which the ear was removed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But when you're teaching your students, as an experienced pathologist and forensic doctor, when you're teaching them what an amputation is, what do you tell them?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: "Amputation" represents the removal of a part of the body or an organ in the body. It can be caused by violence, by which we imply various mechanical forces such as a traffic accident, a knife, a blunt object; or it can be a result of a medical procedure, which is very common. In that case, an organ is removed for therapy reasons or in order to try and save a life if that part of the body or that organ is the source of heavy bleeding. And as for the types of amputation, an amputation can be either complete or incomplete, as I've already stated, or partial, and that will be that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to point to any example in the professional literature or indeed at any time in your professional career where you or any doctor has referred to an amputation performed by mice or other small rodents?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: An example -- I can't think of an example at this moment, but this is not a mistake to call it that, if that is what you're referring to. In this particular case, I did not have any mechanism in mind.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you use the same term, "amputation," to refer to the cutting of the left ear and the cutting of the right ear?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I used the same term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when it came to the left ear -- sorry, the right ear and the damage to it, did you ever offer an opinion prior to today that that may have been caused by small animals?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No. This was mentioned only in my conversation with the Prosecutor when we analysed some of these wounds in somewhat greater detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But analysing them in 2005 is one thing. At the time when you looked at that wound, it was your opinion, wasn't it, that that ear had been cut off after death with some sharp object like a knife. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I was as explicit as that. I -- the only thing that I said explicitly was that the wound occurred after the death of the person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But I'm not referring to what you made explicit in your report, Doctor, but what your honest state of mind was at the time. And at the time when you analysed that, it was your opinion that that was caused by a sharp-bladed instrument after death. Is that correct? And I'm speaking of the right ear.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I did not insist on that particular thing so much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was your -- however, I'm talking about your state of mind, not what you insisted upon to other people, but your own state of mind. That appeared to you at the time, didn't it, to be a cut by a sharp implement after death. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know how you can describe my state of mind. I told you what I knew at the time and what I did, and I just wouldn't dwell upon that. I never implied something that could not be confirmed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. But why did you choose the term "amputate" when it comes to the right ear rather than expressing the view that it could have been caused by small animals?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: The term, as I have already told you, is not wrong and it does not imply a mechanism by which the amputation occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: It was not my wish to imply anything. I always try to be as professional as possible and stick only to the professional aspect of my work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Were you asked at the time of the inspection of Martin Ratkic to comment on whether or not the ear injury on the left-hand side had been inflicted during life or after death?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: In my briefing we discussed this wound, and it was only yesterday.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at the time when you made the inspection, you didn't have any opinion as to whether that ear was cut off during life or not. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No, it's not correct. I just did not state that specifically. As I said in the introduction, the most important thing was to establish the cause of death. Given the fact that the ear wasn't the cause of death, I did not analyse these particular wounds in detail.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we've nearly finished with this topic, but I do have to press you a little bit further. Under the heading of "Opinion" you did put two out of I think it's a total six sentences on the question of these ears. In other words, they were of sufficient significance to you to comment about that in the concluding paragraph, the opinion, and to give some details. At that time, the details you chose to give were that both ears had been amputated, and you used the technical term "amputated." So in light of that, I return to my original question for the final time to ask you this: Now looking back on it and recalling your state of mind, do you agree that you chose the term that you did, "amputated," because it looked to you like the right ear had been cut off after death? And I don't mean what's implicit in what you said here, I mean in your own mind at the time you looked at it.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: You are trying to implant into my brain something that has nothing whatsoever to do with my brain. In my findings I described the wounds that I found on the body and in no way did I imply the mechanism by which they were inflicted. I provided more detail about the gunshot wounds, which were the cause of death, and that is why two-thirds of the text under the heading "Opinion" covered the gunshot wounds. It was not my desire -- it was not the state of my mind that made me write something that wasn't true. I just wanted to describe what I found on the body and the condition it was in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which is the medical dictionary you use most frequently, Doctor?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you are referring to. What dictionary?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if you were required now to go and look up a term, a medical term, and give a dictionary definition for the use of your students or perhaps for this Court, what dictionary would you turn to? What's the name of the dictionary that you would use?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I speak Croatian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: And in our medical dictionary which we use, there are a lot of words that come from Latin, they originate from Latin but they have been adapted to the Croatian language. And just like in English, they have become an integral part of the Croatian dictionary. As far as I know, the same is the case in English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. What's the name of that dictionary and, if you can recall, who were the authors of it?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: The authors of the dictionary?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. The name of the dictionary first; the authors of the dictionary second.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want you to tell me what's the name of the leading medical dictionary that you use, the title of that book.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I use a number of dictionaries, but I don't know their names. I really don't understand what you're asking me. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well -- I mean, you've been called here as an expert with many years' experience, and what I want to know is: What is the name of the leading dictionary that you as a professional turn to in order to define terms or in order to look up the meaning of a particular word?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: It's the dictionary of terms used by all the medical textbooks. Any special dictionary, I really wouldn't know the title. Every area of medicine has its own terminology that it uses, the basis of which is Latin, which has been adopted in all of our textbooks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well -- but, with respect to your particular field of expertise, what is the book to which one turns to find the meaning of terms, words such as "amputation"?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: There are various books pertaining to that area. In ones you will find one definition; in others, you will find another definition.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to assist us, though, can you tell us the names of one or two of these books where these definitions are found?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: There is forensic pathology for medical students. There is a number of textbooks. And in my education I have used a lot of books that are only in English because they have been printed in the English-speaking part of the world.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of course. But if one of your students was researching the meaning of the word "amputation," to what textbook would you refer?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I would refer him to a Latin dictionary to check the word amputatio or amputationis, and that would be that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would there be any medical dictionary or textbook to which you would refer them in relation to the medical term "amputation"?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to recommend a specific dictionary, but I would refer them to specific textbooks where the topic of amputation was covered, the types of amputation, definitions, and so on. A definition for a surgeon is one, and the definition for a pathologist is different. They're similar but there are differences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the past, have you yourself ever referred to an amputation performed by animals?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Why not?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what occasion did you speak about an amputation that was performed by animals?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: When we're talking about shark bites, for example.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And have you dealt with shark bite victims yourself?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you suggesting that that's the way in which you used the term here? Is that your evidence, that when you used the term "amputate" here, you meant it to cover the situation of animal bites to the ear of Martin Ratkic, victim of a shooting in Uzdol?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Animal bites are a possible cause of amputation; that's how I understand it. This is simply possible. This is not the wrong application of a term.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Turning to the left ear now, you indicated that there was what you described as contusions, indicating that this ear had been cut off during life. Now, I have some questions for you about that. Looking at the photograph of Martin Ratkic, deceased as he was, it's obvious that he had been resting with that side of his head, that being the left-hand side, in a downwards position. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: The translation perhaps was not adequate, so I don't know what you mean the term "resting."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well -- very well. It's quite obvious that there's some level of post-mortem lividity fixed on the left-hand side of his head. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. These would be so-called spots, death spots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's also the case that his skin is folded and pressured into a particular pattern of ridges that can be viewed in that photograph because of the effect of gravity and the pressure of his head pressed on that skin. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The left side of his face shows a region that is pale. That is the place where he was leaning on or resting on the surface. And what's around, these things around that pale spot, are the death spots which are caused as a consequence of the blood flow following death.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and in particular it's caused by the operation of gravity, that loose blood collects at the lowest part of the body or in that part of the body. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Due to gravity, all parts of the body that are close to the surface collect the blood, or these death spots are caused, which are a purple-blue colour, while the places of pressure are pale.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, it's also apparent that the left-hand side of Martin Ratkic's face was washed for pathological -- for the purposes of pathologists. Do you agree with that? I don't mean completely washed but partially washed.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the washing is done only after the clothing is completely removed. So we can use the term "wiped" rather than the term "washed off" in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, well, I'm comfortable with you using that term. So what you'd say is that Martin Ratkic at this stage, still being clothed, had been the subject of some level of wiping for your own purposes of examination. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's also evident from that photograph that some blood or bloodstained fluid has made its way from Martin or from the body of Martin not just onto his clothes but onto the steel surface of the tray on which he lies. When you've had a look at that, can you indicate whether you agree or disagree with what I've said.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Some of the blood has already trickled down to the surface itself, but you have to be very careful when you're analysing this picture. This would be the 23rd deceased in the order and perhaps this blood could be there from the previous body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I wanted to ask you about that. I understand that you're under some time pressure, but because of the need to take proper photographs what I suggest is that you, or your attendants, at least, would certainly have cleaned the steel surface of the tray before placing a new person on it for analysis. Partly in order, I'd suggest -- perhaps I'll put the question to you generally, but -- I'll withdraw the question and I'll put another proposition to you. You don't want the signs of putrefaction from one body to be seen on another body. For example, maggots, worms, or other small insects that may have come to dwell in the body, and therefore you clean the slab down before you put a new body down. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: We were using two slabs. One was used to prep the deceased and the other one I used to examine the body. So I cannot tell you specifically whether each table was completely clean before a new body was placed on it. You must understand that in this type of examination, it is not so important to have the blood samples that were found on the body or the table to be looked at because we don't have the danger here of mixing samples because that is not that type of investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I -- and let me indicate I'm not challenging you on that point at all, so that's not a battle we have to fight. What I'm asking you about here is -- to the extent that reddish fluid, either blood or blood-filled water, can be observed in that photograph, that certainly doesn't indicate any bleeding from Martin Ratkic because he'd been dead for days. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it doesn't mean that the person was bleeding, no. But what you need to know is that a body that has been there for a while, there is fluid that is formed in the lungs. And as you can see here, this fluid can then seep out through the mouth and the nose if the body is turned in the process of transport. So it is very difficult to talk about any kind of bleeding. From this aspect we cannot really be precise about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, I understand what you say about that. And what I'm turning to now is the contusions that you have pointed to with respect to this left ear. Would you please take the pointer and point to those on the screen so that the learned Judges can see where you identified contusions.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: The contusions can be seen much better on the original photographs.
