You can't really see them very well here, but you can see it along the edges of the wound and at the bottom of the wound, the bottom edge of the wound. And they are not indicating any signs of post-mortem changes. There are no --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm asking you to consider --

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: -- and this is visible on the right ear, but it's not visible on the left ear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, just a moment. What -- are you suggesting that there are post-mortem changes visible on the right ear or not? I'm dealing at the moment with the left ear.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. I am making a comparison.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, just remaining with the left ear at the moment. By "contusion" you mean swelling, don't you, sometimes accompanied by a redness. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No, you're not correct. A contusion is a -- a crushing or pressure applied on the tissues. It's the place where due to pressure from some kind of force, small blood vessels burst. And this causes damage to the tissues and bleeding in the tissue. When we have this appear on the skin, it will look like a bruise. Subcutaneously, however, it is an area that is splattered or streaked with blood and its edges are blunted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But in order to establish whether you're dealing with a bruise or a contusion of the type that you've just described, you really need to do some sort of histological analysis involving the use of slides and microscopic equipment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No, that is not required; that can only confirm what you are seeing. But additional tests are hardly ever carried out in order to see something that is already very evident to any competent pathologist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But what we're dealing with here is an inference that you have suggested that the contusions there suggest that the ear was cut off in life, and that's what I'm dealing with with you now. First of all, are you able to point to a contusion that lies directly upon the cutting line or the severing line of the ear in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Most precisely stated, it would be along the edges of the wound and in the depth of the wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, my question is: Is that depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is depicted in the photograph, but of course it was much better to see it live as it actually was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But let's just stick with the photograph for a moment. Are you suggesting that the cutting line is visible in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: The cutting line is partially visible. You cannot see the back of the side of the cutting. We can strictly stick to the photograph, but then we can draw the wrong conclusions, just as you previously saw blood, which we can draw certain conclusions about but it's also possible that our conclusions would be wrong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's okay. We'll come to the conclusions in a minute. I just need to establish the facts first, and the facts at the moment are you've said that there is -- the edge of the cutting wound is partially visible. What I'd ask -- would you just excuse me a moment, please, Doctor, we have a technical issue we have to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like the witness to mark with a red marker, if that's possible, as we have done in previous situations, with a circle where this cutting line is. I don't know if that's possible with the technology if we're in Sanction at the moment. I'm not sure where we are really in technological terms. So I'm just inquiring of the court staff if they can help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't think this photo is in the e-court system.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, this photograph has not been uploaded into the e-court system so we have only a hard copy of this at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will ask the witness to mark my hard copy and I'll just tender it as a hard copy. I think the time has come to tear it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, I'll just provide you with my copy, I think mine is unmarked, but you feel free to mark that any way you want. What I would like you to do, if you wouldn't mind, is to draw a circle around the area where you say the cutting edge can be seen. So don't draw over the cutting edge under any circumstances, but just draw, if you like, an oval or a circle around it so we can see where it is for ourselves.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I will use a blue pen. This is where the visible edge starts. It goes upwards. Here it becomes indistinct because of the hair. The hair in this place is covering the edge, so we lose a whole section here which was under the hair and we cannot analyse it on the photograph. Then we have the bottom edge here, and that then goes on to the posterior of the head. The lower part indicates a fragment of the ear that remained. But it's very difficult to analyse the edge here because of the angle, because, in a way, the edge is on the bottom. So that is why we are only seeing parts of the edge. Its visible parts are one-third to one-quarter. We are unable to analyse the part that is covered by the hair, and this other part is not possible to analyse because the cutting edge is facing down; it's on the bottom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Now I understand that. Now, looking at that picture there, you would point to the pinkish area to the right of that cut as being a contusion, supporting the hypothesis that the cut happened during life. Am I right so far?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: This part here and along the bottom edges. Yes, you are right there, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to the part that you referred to along the bottom edges that you're talking about, please, that you say is a contusion. You've indicated that round part in the middle, I understand that. But you also indicated something along the bottom edges. Is that visible in the picture; and if so, can you point it out.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: You can see that in this part here, that's along the very edge, under the skin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. Well, I understand what you say about that. Now, let me put this proposition to you: It's quite possible, isn't it, that that contusion could have been easily caused by some other blow or contact before death and that the ear cutting itself occurred after death. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I would not agree with that. I think that you can clearly see here the contusions which are distributed all along the bottom edge. So that possibility is quite remote.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, first of all, it is a possibility that you can't discount, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: In many cases when I testify at court my assertions are not 100 per cent certain. You always have to be -- leave some room for circumstances in life or medicine. And that is why I am saying as a possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in this case I suggest to you that possibility is augmented and increased by the fact that this man obviously at some stage was resting with that side of his head in a downward position, thus bringing to that side of his head loose blood, which may itself account for some level of swelling in that area. Do you agree with that possibility?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No. It is clear here that you didn't understand me properly. The death spots which are caused do not cause swelling. They just are a pooling of the blood which drops there. It is collected there due to the force of gravity. This does not cause contusions of the tissue. On the other hand, you are probably trying to understand in some way that the person, after sustaining some wounds, fell on that side and hit his ear. In this case, I would have to rule out this possibility with quite a high degree of certainty, because in that case there would be contusions on his face, also abrasions, which would be visible on the face. Here you can see that this part of the -- this protruding part of the features, which we call the cheekbone, which would make contact first with the surface, do not show such injuries. So we cannot find any traces of external injuries around the ear. So therefore we can assume that this blood that collected there could not have been caused in that way. That would only be in the area of the ear. It would be -- cover a broader surface. It would be in front of the ear, below the ear, or around the ear. And also you would see the signs of abrasions, injuries, and swellings on other parts of the skin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There --

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: And that is why --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, if I could just stop you there to deal with what you've raised. Aren't there two difficulties with that: First of all, you or your assistants wiped that face, didn't you, wiped it clean, to some degree at all events, of whatever was on it.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And secondly, you're inferring that the person fell on a particularly flat surface and must therefore have banged their cheekbone. But in any event, what's that black dot right in the middle of the cheekbone there?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: It is a blood clot or it's just a bloodstain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, how did that blood get there?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: It got there, as you can see from the mouth, the nose, and also perhaps from the area of the ear. What I have to say to the Court is that after these photographs were made, we unclothed the body completely and washed it more thoroughly. So my opinion is not only based on these photographs but also on all the other details that I noticed during my examination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are there any notes of those other observations?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I stated that in my finding.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just wanted to put a definition from Black's Medical Dictionary, 39th edition, edited by Gordon Macpherson. It's a book found in the ICTY library here and it's published by Madison Books 1999, and it defines amputation this way: "Amputation: Severance of a limb, or part of a limb from the rest of the body. The leg is the most common sight of amputation. It is usually performed as a controlled operation and may be required for a variety of reasons. In the young, severe injury is the most common cause, when damage to the limb is so extensive as to make it non-viable or functionally --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down. The interpreters cannot --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Pardon me. "... to make it non-viable or functionally useless. In the elderly, amputation is more often the result of vascular insufficiency, resulting in gangrene or intractable pain. "The aim is to restore the patient to full mobility with a prosthetic (artificial) limb, which requires both a well-fitting prosthesis and a well-healed surgical wound. If this is not possible, the aim is to leave the patient with a limb stump that is still useful for balancing, sitting and transferring. Common types of lower-limb amputations are shown in the illustration --" which I'll show you in a minute. "The Symes amputation can be walked upon without requiring a prosthesis. Below-the-knee amputation preserves normal flexion of the knee, and virtually normal walking can be achieved with a well-fitting artificial limb. Learning to walk is more difficult following an above-knee amputation, but some well-motivated patients can manage well." I've nearly finished. "After any amputation it is not unusual for the patient to experience the sensation that the limb is still present. This is called a phantom limb and the sensation may persist for a long time." And then it's got a further note saying, "(See prosthesis, phantom limb.)" Now, is that definition one that you accept as a proper definition for the term "amputation," bearing in mind your many years of medical practice and teaching responsibilities and professorships?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: If you go back to the first sentence, then the author defined amputation very much similar to the way I did, saying that this is a complete or partial removal of organs or parts of a body.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but it doesn't normally include eating the part that you're talking about, does it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour. This has been asked and answered ad nauseam. This definition is not inconsistent with his statement, and as a result it's irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, if at least we spend 40 minutes on the definition of "amputation" and that issue --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, we did and you can see why it's a matter of relevance and interest to the Defence. But never before has this thesis emerged, now it does, and I really want to test it as hard as I can. It couldn't be said under any circumstances to be irrelevant, but although I don't agree with my learned friend's objection, if Your Honour thinks it's been asked enough times and that it's become repetitive, then that's the end of it. Because I referred to a medical dictionary -- medical dictionaries earlier on and asked, for quite a while, actually, whether we could be referred to one, I thought it was fair to put it, I've put it, and that was the extent of what was going to be put, frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I believe the testimony of this witness can either go to the truth or go to the credibility. So in this sense that you have achieved your purpose already.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've asked as many questions as -- frankly, as even I consider legitimate and that's the end of the questions on that topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However, returning to this left ear, you would agree with me about this, wouldn't you, that never before did you say -- I'm talking about the left ear now. That never before did you say that was cut off during life until you got to The Hague. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: When I was interviewed in Croatia, nobody ever asked me about the mechanism by which the amputation of the ear or both ears occurred. This was not considered important at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a second. You knew that you had to complete these autopsies in a hurry, partially because officials of the Herceg-Bosna wanted to hold a press conference concerning these matters. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Whenever we were working in Bosnia or when we did something to do with Bosnia, there was always a pressure of time due to the war circumstances, and we had to work at a very fast pace and hand the bodies over to their families. Our contacts with the representatives of the government and the families were mostly through my associate, Dr. Ivanovic. He also talked to the families of the deceased as well as the representatives of the local authorities. He had contacts with all these people. And he would pass on messages to us in the operating theatre. At that time while we were involved in the post-mortems, we did not know anything about a press conference. We were in the OR all day, and the only break we had was sometime in the afternoon when we had something that one might call lunch.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we please go to autopsy report number 26. This concerns Anica Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I think one of the photographs was marked and there's no note of it being on the record what the ERN is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Are you going to tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I guess there's no objections from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: While I'm up here, Your Honour, can I put for the record the two photographs that were mentioned previously at the end of examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Photograph relating to victim number 6 was 0361-7360, and the photograph as to victim number 26 was 0361-7474. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Mr. Morrissey, I was told that this photograph is not marked yet. Do you want this witness to mark it again or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, what I would prefer is to do it on the e-court if that's possible and I'm not sure what is proposed about that in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that for this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But I think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: -- it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the fact is I've asked questions about it so we can't leave it hanging. If we can't do it on the e-court later, I should do it now and just return to that site, means a return to the ear, but perhaps we should do it immediately. So I will ask that that be returned to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I just ask that he circle, as indicated, the area where the cutting line that he discerns there is to be found.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Doctor, earlier on you demonstrated by using the point of the pen, but you didn't actually leave a mark on the page. We've got a number of copies of that, so feel free. Could you just put a circle around the area that you indicated as being where the cutting can be seen.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: This line depicts the place where the border can be seen, then the line is interrupted because of the presence of the hair. We can see the bottom in the photo, and then it continues in the lower part. And in this part, as I've already told you, the borders are underneath and cannot be analysed, and one part of the ear is missing here. In this part here, we can see the preserved part of the earlobe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well, thank you for doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, now I offer that to be tendered in its marked form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, it's admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could I ask the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Morrissey. That will be exhibit D414.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we please just go -- Doctor, would you mind going now to Anica Stojanovic, whose body was examined as Uzdol number 26. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this instance could you please turn to the section "Patho-anatomical Diagnosis." Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that the third topic that you've raised there is a topic "animal bite to right lower leg." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now can I ask you to go and have a look at the next category down, which is "Cause of Death," and do we notice there on cause of death no reference whatsoever to the animal bite. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Only the main diagnosis is put here, the one that actually caused the death.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certainly. Now go to the heading of Opinion. You see the heading "Opinion."

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you please look at the last paragraph -- last section of that opinion, where you say this: "There is a gunshot wound to the right lower leg and wounds caused by animal bites, most likely those of small rodents." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw animal bites by small rodents, you put it in your reports, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And although here in The Hague you've analysed the possibility of the ear being bitten off Martin Ratkic by small rodents, what I'm suggesting to you is that's only a thought that has occurred to you in conversation with my learned friend the Prosecutor, Mr. Weiner. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: This has been asked and answered and I want him to put a basis for that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Remove the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If he wants to, let him remove the witness. If he's going to make an accusation about me, let him remove the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm not making any accusations at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No I think the Defence is entitled to know some background informations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I should make it clear, so there's no false controversy, I'm not accusing Mr. Weiner of anything improper at all in asking this question. The question is: This topic first came up in discussions with the Prosecutor. It's a timing question, and that's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The thesis that that ear came off courtesy of some small animals first came up when you spoke to Mr. Weiner. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: This is not the first time it appeared. It was then when we spoke about the mechanism by which the wounds occurred. Your claim is partially correct but partially incorrect. This was not a new creation. We just analysed the mechanism, which was not mentioned previously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was it that you mentioned the mechanism of Ana Stojanovic's wound to the lower leg courtesy of animal bites in the report that you did on Anica Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I mentioned it with the intention to describe the wound. There was nothing special to it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, if there was the faintest chance that Martin Ratkic's ear was nibbled on by animals, why didn't you mention that in exactly the same way?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I simply didn't. I did not have any intentions. In that report, I did not mention the mechanism by which the amputation of any of the ears occurred. I just didn't do it. It was not on purpose. It just so happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, since we're on Anica Stojanovic right now, I just want to ask you some questions about her. In this Tribunal there's been evidence given, somebody said they saw her being killed. But what you observed was a number of bullet wounds to Anica Stojanovic when you came to analyse her. Is that correct? Not one but a number. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: You can find it in my report; it's all there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. But just tell us anyway. How many shots entered her body?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: There is the cause of death wound, which is on the head, the gunshot wound of the head, and then we also have the wound in the chest -- actually in the -- the entrance wound is in the front part of the chest and the exit wound is on the back part.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have got a useful diagram. I understand these diagrams are not meant to be entirely precise. Would you be able to indicate to the Tribunal, just pointing to your own chest, approximately where that entry wound was on the chest?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Judging by the description, it was in the back, on the back side. And the exit wound was on the right-hand side of the chest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So effectively a shot from the back that came out on the right-hand side of the front. Correct? So it's a shot that would cause catastrophic injuries to the lungs and probably to the heart as well. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Given the height, it would sooner be in the lungs and the internal organs rather than in the heart.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Because the heart is somewhat higher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It's just a little difficult from the pictures to be sure exactly where on the body that took place. Could I just ask you to look, please -- I'll hold up the photograph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, could we have a break at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honours. Just in order to finish with this particular deceased person, might I just ask a two more quick questions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: -- and then Anica Stojanovic is finished. I apologise for going on at this length. Your Honours, I'm just going to hold up -- because we don't have the e-court working, I'm just going to hold up this picture so that the witness can see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I have no problem with him holding up a picture, but can he identify the number so we have it on the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's what I can't do, because the ones I've got don't have numbers. If I hold it up -- it's got a number 26, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, there's an ERN number at the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, I'm grateful for the correction. I do have that. The one I'm showing is 0361-7475.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll just hold it up so you can see, Doctor, which one I'm looking at. Yes. Thank you. Would you mind explaining which wound is depicted there in that photograph concerning Anica Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: This is not one of my originals. I don't have that original.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What -- can you make any comment about that because, Doctor, all we have on the Defence side is what we are provided by the Prosecutor and I dare say what they've been provided with by your institution. Do you -- although that is not one of your photos, is it a photo that you recognise? 11

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: It's very difficult for me to say that I recognise the photo. I recognise the number and the way the photo is marked, but not the photo itself, I'm afraid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Before I provide you with my opinion, I would like to know whether this is an original photo like one of the originals that I have with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, look, I'm sorry. If I can put it colloquially, you're talking to the wrong man here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think it's probably best to take he break because this is a photograph the doctor hasn't seen, so it's not fair to him put it to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Let's take a break, and we'll resume at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just indicate there's a bit of a mystery about this photograph. The Prosecutors don't seem to have it and the witness doesn't know about it. At this point what we might do is just leave it and we'll make an inquiry later on to see if we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What I might do is just ask the witness:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Doctor, in relation to that photograph that I showed you earlier, you're not -- because of being under cross-examination, you can't consult with anyone else, but could I provide you with a copy of it and if it turns out that you've got some sort of copy --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm happy to hand this over now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if it matches anything that's in your notes, would you mind indicating that to us, perhaps tomorrow. I won't press you about now it if it's not a document you've seen before, but maybe when you have time, have a look and see what the situation is with it. If it fits anywhere, I'll ask you questions; and if not, we won't. Okay, so I've asked you about Anica Stojanovic and we've now dealt with Martin Ratkic and Anica Stojanovic. Before I move on to the others, so many of the others as I'm going to ask questions about, I've got some general questions about the autopsy procedure that you followed here. It's a fact that you performed a relatively full autopsy on young Stjepan Zelic, who was only about 10 years old. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I think in his case, because you looked at the wound tracks within the body and because you were able to spend some time on him, you formed a view that at least one of the projectiles that hit him did so at a time when he was toppling to the ground or falling to the ground, thus allowing a bullet to enter his body on two separate occasions in the one flight. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: The same projectile, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I understand. And -- yes. Okay. Apart from Stjepan Zelic, did you spend approximately 20 minutes to half an hour on each other person?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I can't be certain of that. It was a long time ago. Some bodies required more time for description because they had more wounds and some bodies required less time for the same reason; they had less wounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I appreciate it's not right to put an average figure on it, but is it accurate to say that the -- those bodies that had more wounds you might have allowed 30 to 40 minutes and those who had less wounds you might have allowed 20 to 30 minutes? These are approximate figures, but are they accurate within that?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Again, whatever I told you would be just my approximation. It was a long time ago and I can't give you any -- anything with any degree of certainty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. In peacetime when dealing with a single murder victim, let's say a person who was hit by two to three bullets, what's the range of time that you would like to allow yourself to perform a full autopsy?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: About an hour or an hour and a quarter or an hour and a half. It would all depend on the simplicity of the findings, whether the findings are simple or whether some of the findings have to be additionally examined. Most of the time in peacetime autopsies one spends in taking a dual set of photos; one set for the police and one set for the department, and this is what takes up most of the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In dealing with these autopsies, and I'm not talking about Stjepan Zelic but the other 26, tell me if the following propositions are correct: First of all, all of the bodies were to some degree afflicted by putrefaction and post-death change. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct. All the bodies demonstrated a certain degree of post-mortem changes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Secondly, with respect to the remaining 26 bodies, you performed no analysis of the internal path taken by any of the lethal projectiles, bullets. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I made my conclusions based on the entry and exit wounds. I did not perform an internal examination, an examination of the internal organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thirdly, you did not nor were you in a position to collect any bullets or projectiles for subsequent forensic analysis. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you provided by the authorities with any projectiles or any other items which were said to be connected with the cause of death, such as bullets or other weapons?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in a position to swab any of the wounds which appeared to have powder marks or burn marks in their proximity in order to submit those for subsequent chemical testing?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: This is a very good question. However, you forget that it was the time of war and that our autopsies were performed in conditions close to war conditions. And to your question, I would like to answer by putting you another question: What would I have done with such samples? Nobody would have been able to pay for any such analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let it be quite clear that that question wasn't meant to contain any criticism at all, and I understand that there was a war on. But the answer to my question is that that wasn't done. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And indeed it just wasn't a feasible thing to consider doing at the time. Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I understand that. Are you familiar with the sort of tests that I'm -- or the sort of procedure I'm talking about where in some cases it's possible to take a swab of powder for subsequent gunshot residue or indeed other chemical types of test?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm quite familiar with that procedure. I was educated to do that, and not only can you perform a chemical analysis, you can also perform an electronic microscope analysis which can confirm the origin of the gunpowder particles and compare those with the gunpowder from the possible weapon from which the crime may have been committed. Also, you can do the so-called paraffin glove test, by which you take the sample of gunpowder particles from the perpetrator's hand and those are compared with the weapon and the particles found on the body or on the clothes of the victim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I understand that. And could I just pursue that a little bit further. Did you notice whether or not any gunshot residue or other crime scene residue could be discerned on the clothing or the hair of any of the victims that you encountered?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Residue of gunpowder particles could be seen around the edges of the wounds, as I have already explained in my drawing. They present themselves as the blackish-greyish impregnation or the tattoo-like spots on the skin. You can see those on the pictures in some of the cases described herein. And especially in wounds which were inflicted from a very close range or mid-range.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And with respect to those marks that you see on wounds like that, you've indicated two quite distinct phenomena which I want to ask you about. The first one concerns the gunshot residue and the second one concerns the burning marks. Now, it's a fact that on a particular wound you might get either or both or, of course, none of those phenomena, depending on how close the person is to the weapon that gets shot. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: To a certain extent, yes. You are covering a pretty wide range --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: -- but you are right to a certain degree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was an introductory question, and I understand it sounds babyish. As to the burning effect, the extent to which you can estimate how close the gun was to the skin by virtue of burn marks is very much a function of the nature of the firearm used in the particular case. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Only partially. That is only partially correct and I would like you to specify what you mean by the burning effect or the burn marks. These burns --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, the -- just -- sorry, go on.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: -- are not classical ones. This is something that we find at the bottom of the wound. It would be like soot or -- so that the term "burned" is inappropriate here, even though it is caused from the flame that comes from a firearm if it is quite close.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And what's the effect on a wound of a tracer bullet, in particular of the trail of a tracer bullet?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: The question is not clear to me. Could you please -- what do you mean by "tracer bullet"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Some bullets leave a trail that's visible to the eye of burning or combustible material, leaving a path that can be seen and may in some cases leave a mark. Do you have experience of such a bullet, a tracer bullet, one of those bullets that discharges a combustible stream of some sort behind it, causing a wound? And if so, what sort of wound does it cause? Does it leave burning?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: In my work on these 27 cases did not find indications that tracer bullets were used, whereby the burn marks would be primary traces or markings. These were classic projectiles fired at close range or at a -- from a distance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the existence of three or four days' of putrefaction of the body assist or hinder in your ability to accurately comment on how close the gun was to the body when it was fired?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Of course it makes it more difficult, and I did put that in some of the reports.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you and I acknowledge that you did, and that's one of the reasons I'm asking the question. And in what ways is putrefaction a negative factor in performing that analysis?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Putrefaction is an adverse factor in the sense that if a certain amount of time passed, then there would no longer be any soft tissue left, so we would not be able to make that analysis. On the other hand, putrefaction discolours the skin and it causes secondary changes on all tissues in the sense that gases collect and similar changes occur which make analysis more difficult. Other than that, very quickly the bodies are invaded by larvae which can then -- of maggots, which can then completely destroy the tissue so that the tissue would then no longer be fit for analysis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Now, I'm just going to take you to some specific deceased persons now. Just forgive me while I assemble this. Did you have at that time available to you a laboratory that could perform histology, analysis of skin samples and so forth?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the time we did have a lab for histological analysis of skin samples, but this type of testing is very expensive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it exactly the same situation that we dealt with when we were talking about the gunshot residue, that although you had -- in theory you had the resources, in practice you just couldn't use them because of the war?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Not only that, but the question -- the fact that we had a large number of such cases was one thing; on the other hand, nobody paid for this. Also, labs which were able to carry out that kind of analysis of samples, gunpowder samples, were not located in our area. We would have to ask for outside expert opinions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now --

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we don't want to leave the impression that histological testing would shed more light on these cases. I just want to clarify that. Pathological and histological findings are already known when we have wounds like these, so no new information could be gleaned from those kinds of analyses. But analysis of the gunpowder residue could tell us what type of weapon was in question, but a histological analysis would just confirm what we could actually see with the plain eye; that these were in fact gunshot wounds.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you performed these autopsies, were you asked to consider the question of whether or not any of these people had been killed by artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody asked us to say that -- to do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no. Was the topic one that occurred to you to deal with in the course of your analyses?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Of course I thought about that. And as I said, I could tell that some wound had been caused by a fragment of an explosive device because in such devices we would have shattering of the -- when we're talking about artillery weapons, such an effect would be even greater.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. But what happened hand grenades? Did you see the possibility that somebody might have been injured by a hand grenade? And in particular now I'm thinking of Ruza Zelenika, whose -- the top of whose head was badly damaged in her or near to her bed, as was shown in the photograph earlier on in the day.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: As I said before at the beginning of my testimony, such a wound caused by an explosive device would appear differently. It would have irregular edges, it would have dirt and -- that happened to be around. It would have traces of fabric or any other matter that would be impacted into the wound. So such a wound would have completely different appearance and characteristics from those that were described in this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I have a question for you about what you meant by distant shots. When you describe a shot as being distant, does that mean it's anything between 1 metre and the total range of the gun?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and by that I am thinking of a distance greater than 1 metre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: And to be perhaps more precise --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I cut you off. Keep going.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: We cannot say where it is coming from but whether it has enough kinetic energy to cause a wound of a certain type.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. In this case, Doctor, there's three deceased persons; Stjepan Zelic, he's your number one, victim number one; his mother, Ruza Zelic, your victim number two; and his sister, Maria Zelic, who was only 13 years old, and she's victim number 19. In each of those cases it appears that you've referred to distant shots -- feel free to look, and the Prosecution will correct if it's not right. But in each case I believe you've referred to distant shots there.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I should actually look at it case by case, so I would ask you to put your questions to me in that way so we could be more efficient.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, that's okay. I'm going to ask you to deal with them one by one. Did you know or was it explained to you that those three had been found together, killed on a road relatively close to each other?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't informed about that. And if my department was informed of that, that information did not reach me. So perhaps Dr. Jovanovic knew about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's okay. All right. Well, in any event, when you say Stjepan Zelic was killed by a shot that's distant, or shots that were distant, that could be anything between 1 and any -- 1 and hundreds of metres away?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And the same goes for Ruza Zelic, who is victim number two, distant shots; and Marija Zelic, who is victim number 19, distant shots. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's identical for all of them, from a distance, yes. That's them. Probably it ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: People who take a shot who were hit in the chest, in your experience, may die very quickly or they may linger for some minutes before the mechanism of death sets in. Is that correct, in your experience?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct. Some of them even survive if they are treated adequately. It depends on the damage the projectile inflicts. If a major blood vessel is damaged, death will follow very quickly. If lungs are damaged, a person can live for a long time with damage to the lungs and they can remain alive for quite a long time. So it depends on the type of injuries to the internal organs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And so in the abstract, one thing that is possible is that a person may be fatally wounded but they may still live for some minutes or even in some cases for longer than that altogether. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: If adequate treatment is given, then they can survive. But of course there is a difference in how long somebody would live once they sustain a serious injury, and that depends on the speed with which a person bleeds or how the injured organs react to the injury.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I suppose the abstract or the hypothetical I'm putting to you now is: If a person's shot and they collapse to the ground and crack their head on the ground when they fall, then they may well develop bruising because they're still alive where they fell down, even though they die subsequently. They might live long enough to display some -- to develop bruising and display some signs of bruising after they're dead. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. And we can conclude that for as long as the blood circulation is functioning, there is the possibility of contusions, bruises appearing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. All right. Now, can I move on now to the next people -- well, I won't ask you about the distant shots people, but there's some that I -- who it's relevant to ask about. Ruza Zelenika I've already asked a couple of questions. This is your number 6. Could we just have on the screen, please -- would you just excuse me a moment. Exhibit P312 at 36 minutes and 39 seconds. I'm just going to show you that photograph of the woman Ruza Zelenika who had evidently suffered terrible injuries on or near to that bed. I would just ask that the image be held when it reaches that point of displaying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecutors are offering to help by putting it in Sanction. I think in order to keep things moving I'm very grateful for that and we'll use that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There we are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just having regard to that, it's evident to you from that photograph, isn't it, that there's some pinkish-grey matter that's been sprayed on the wall and that, in addition, there are two large round holes near the corner of that room in the walls. Do you see those?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No. Could you please show me where you're looking at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Don't you have that on the screen? Well, I don't think you can see my screen --

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I see the photograph, but could you please just point to what you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the corner of the wall, do you see the corner of the wall, where the wall turns at a 90-degree angle?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you see perhaps a foot, maybe a foot and a half above the head of the deceased two holes in the wall, which may be bullet holes, they may be some other kind of holes, I don't know, but anyway do you see those holes?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I do see some kind of imperfection but I don't know whether that's a hole or not. Are you thinking of this upper right spot?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking about in the corner of the wall, 18 inches or so above the head of the deceased, you'll see there's a defect in the wall -- in one wall and then there's another defect in the wall about the same height on the adjoining wall. Do you see those holes? It's in the middle left of the picture as a whole.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I see one defect. I don't see another one on that part of the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, at all events I understand you initially formed a view that there was the possibility of some chopping with an axe or similar implement there, but do you acknowledge the possibility that -- now that you've seen this photograph and the marks on the walls, do you acknowledge the possibility that in fact what caused the loss of that part of the head was in fact a burst of gunfire?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I already said that I do allow for that possibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, as to -- as to killings performed by people with axes or heavy implements of some sort, in your career I suppose you must have seen a few crime scenes involving such killings. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in such situations it's very common that you will get a phenomenon called cast-off whereby a blow having been struck, blood is sprayed up the wall by the lifting up of the implement a second time. Are you familiar with that? In English it's called cast-off, but are you familiar with that phenomenon that you might get a line of blood up a wall because a bloody instrument has been swung high?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you notice here in this photograph that although there's various pinkish-coloured marks, there seems to be, in simply the photograph we're looking at, of course, a relative absence of red blood. Is that something that catches your attention or not?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I think that you are incorrect because I think that there are some traces of blood there. I don't know whether there were any changes or not. It's difficult to analyse it like this, but it seems to me that we are seeing some kind of blood here. It's very difficult to make a finding based on a photograph that is of such poor resolution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, with respect, I frankly agree with what you say about that. Very well. Well, those are the questions that I have on that -- for that particular deceased person, and that photograph can now be removed from the screen. Thank you. Victim number 7 was Kata Ljubic. This was a situation where you've indicated I think three distant shots and one that's a relatively close head shot with powder. Now, have regard -- of course you're allowed to have in front of you the report that you wrote about Kata Ljubic, it's number seven. What I wanted to ask you is this: As regards the close-up shot, the head shot, it's not possible to say whether or not Kata Ljubic was alive at the time when that shot was fired, is it?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No, based on the characteristic features of the wound, we could say she was still alive. Again, this is on the basis of the vital signs that we are finding around the wound.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the photograph that we're referring to, I just want to make sure we're looking at the same one, is it this? I just wonder if the witness wouldn't mind holding up the photograph which depicts these vital signs.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a photograph that is numbered 0361-7365.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to say that in that photograph you can see signs of vital signs, you can see an indication of vital signs there rather than simply a defect?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: I do see signs of contusion of the tissue, and this would be a wound that is typically sustained while the person is still alive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Are you able to say whether the other wounds that she sustained were life threatening or likely to prove fatal in the absence of this particular wound?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Given the fact that she had three more entry and three more exit wounds in the chest and in the lower extremities, those are also serious wounds that may have caused her death.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Very well. Just excuse me one moment, please, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Pardon me. I'm sorry about that. All right. The next person I wanted to ask you about is Mijo Rajic. That's victim number 8.

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in the case of Mijo Rajic, I want to ask you a question about whether it looks as if the same -- or perhaps I shouldn't -- I've got some preliminary questions before that. Can I just ask you this: Were you aware of a weapon called an M-48 at that time?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And were you familiar with -- could I ask you this: Without performing an internal examination and in particular without inspecting the lethal projectile, were you in a position with any of these individuals, outside of Stjepan Zelic, to make a comment as to what the weapon was that discharged the projectile?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: All I can say here is that the wounds inflicted by hand-held firearms show certain characteristics, and this was also the case with Kalashnikov or M-45. From the forensic point of view, they looked like wounds inflicted at a close range. The only difference will be in the range at which they can eject gunpowder particles. And as for the characteristics of these particles, they are the same. As I've already said in the introduction, these wounds look very similar if they are inflicted by similar types of firearms. That is why in order to analyse whether a wound was inflicted at a close or a distant range, one doesn't need to perform an internal examination. An internal examination will just tell us about the internal organ lesions that the person suffered and not about the characteristics or the range from which the projectile was fired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Would you just excuse me one moment, please, Doctor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, would you just permit me one moment, I just want to speak to Mr. Halilovic for one moment and then I'll resume. There's no need to seek an adjournment. Could I just approach?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apologies for that, Doctor, but I can indicate this: I'm going to finish tonight as a result of that. Very well. Look, the last issue that I have to raise with you really is this: Do you recall what instructions it was that you received when you dealt with this group of bodies that arrived? In other words, what -- were you simply told, "Perform an autopsy the best way you can," or were you told to concentrate on a specific area?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: Here I have to say that I didn't expect this type of question, however I have to point out one thing: Throughout the war many war victims passed through our hospital and through our department, both living and dead. And irrespective of any religious affiliation of the victims, we did everything professionally to the best of our capabilities and knowledge. And any insinuations as to me having received any instructions save for those to perform my duties are totally out of place. In my work I only used --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop there for a moment. You've misunderstood the question. It's not a question of whether you did anything improper at all, Doctor, and I'm not asking you that question. What I'm asking you is: Were you given any instructions to take an interest in a particular area, such as whether the bodies were mutilated or not?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: No. I did not receive any such instruction. You know that in conflicts there is an inclination to portray things worse than they actually are. However, I as the head of the department and all of my employees never acted in such a way. We never received any political instruction or order to perform autopsies and point out things that could be pointed out in order to put the other side in a worse position. We had two things in mind as our priorities: We wanted to perform our professional part to the best of our abilities at the moment. Can you imagine me with 27 bodies? And if you can, then you will certainly agree that this is some sort of a phenomenon in European terms. And when I told this story to my European and American colleagues, they simply didn't believe me. And we performed those autopsies extremely objectively without any subjectivity whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. I understand that's what you say. And the question wasn't really --

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: In a nutshell, we never received any political instruction. We just received a professional and human instructions to perform those autopsies within the scope of one day. That was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And was that instruction to do it in one day an instruction you had in writing or was it a verbal instruction?

utterances.speaker: SIMUN ANDJELINOVIC
utterances.text: This was something that was said to me verbally, via Dr. Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Yes. Those are the questions. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, it seems to me that we don't have enough time to finish this witness today. So -- well, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you prefer to begin your re-direct today or we leave it tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I think it would be easier if we do it tomorrow morning because I want to show him a couple of little segments of a video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Well, Witness, I'm afraid that you have to stay in The Hague for another day, and I have to remind you that while you are in The Hague you are still under the oath, so do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have been a forensic expert for a number of years and I'm quite familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that the hearing is adjourned for today and will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 13th day of May, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.56 p.m.,
